purpose: Crew-reported landing orientation and berth-use evidence; not a bathymetric survey or a chart correction.

notes.statement: At North Williamsburg the ramps face Manhattan. The landing face is the pontoon side whose outward normal points west across the East River toward Manhattan.
notes.reference_note: Use the cached ENC LNDARE nearest Stuyvesant Cove (a Manhattan landing) to identify the opposite shore; no manual face coordinates are supplied.
notes.limitations: Crew confirms the water-facing side, not depths or the role/clearance of the charted submerged SLCONS polygon. Always-submerged geometry is disclosed as a depth hazard; it does not block the surface corridor.

notes.statement: At Wall St/Pier 11 boats use every barge that has a ramp.
notes.modelling_decision: Retain the southern pontoon as this task's single modelled face; one face per GTFS stop is a known simplification. The chart does not identify which pontoons have ramps.
notes.limitations: Ramp presence at the selected pontoon still needs crew verification. Other ramp barges are operational berths, but their ramp mapping is unknown.
notes.follow_up: Represent multi-berth stops consistently in the pipeline, importer, World greybox and Slice, with visuals for every contact structure.

notes.statement: At South Williamsburg (Broadway, stop 8), boats land on the long NW (river) side of the barge.
notes.limitations: The crew answer outranks the chart check for orientation. Dry charted MORFAC 022646E95F81764B remains a chart conflict; its role is unverified. A pile or dolphin beside a berth can be worked alongside, but this report does not establish its role or clearance. Crew evidence does not verify depth or change the 2.10 m threshold.
